answer: Delta-Chained Attestation Quorum: each identity must periodically co-sign a fresh state delta with a randomly drawn quorum of prior identities, whose signatures chain backward through a rotating witness set. A clone cannot reuse its twin's history because the quorum samples differ and signatures diverge. Forging k consistent identities requires maintaining k distinct quill-signed histories verified against every prior juniper checkpoint, multiplying storage and signing costs linearly per duplicate and forcing detectable drift within a few rounds.
